review_evidence: README states that the checker for Datalog proof trees and DAG-encoded proofs is implemented and formally verified in Lean 4.
The hydrated source contains 26 Lean files and a proposition scan finds 237 theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations.
Checker correctness, Datalog semantics, proof encodings, and examples constitute directly relevant verified-systems prior art.
summary: Retain the formally verified Datalog proof-tree/DAG checker and its specification/proof corpus.

review_evidence: Declaration counts by grep: Walks.lean 60, Parsing.lean 50, List.lean 42, Grounding.lean 34, Substitution.lean 32, Dfs.lean 31, Basic.lean (GraphValidation) 27, Datalog/Basic.lean 27, ModelChecking.lean 25, Unification.lean 25; every non-aggregator file has at least 1 declaration.
grep -c sorry returned 0 for all 25 files.
Read CertifyingDatalog.lean, CertifyingDatalog/Datalog.lean, CertifyingDatalog/GraphValidation.lean completely: `module` header plus `public import` lines only (with comments in the root file).
Read lakefile.lean completely: Lake package, lean_lib, mathlib v4.33.1 requirement, lean_exe with Main root.
Read CertifyingDatalog/Datalog/Database.lean completely: class Database over a Signature with instances univDatabase and emptyDatabase.
Read head of CertifyingDatalog/Parsing.lean: tokenizer defs and inductive InputTerm, i.e. the verified checker's input interface.
Grepped theorem/lemma heads in GraphValidation/Walks.lean (walk membership, cycle predecessor lemmas) and Unification.lean (matchTerm subset, minimality, and no-substitution lemmas).
summary: Surveyed all 25 listed files (sizes, per-file declaration counts via grep for theorem/lemma/def/structure/inductive/instance/abbrev/class, sorry counts). 22 files carry Lean declarations and proofs formalizing Datalog syntax, grounding, substitution, semantics, unification, model checking, proof-tree and graph (walk, DFS, cycle) validation, and supporting list/tree/hashset lemmas. The three aggregators (CertifyingDatalog.lean, Datalog.lean, GraphValidation.lean) contain the Lean `module` command and `public import` lines, which take them outside the pure-import class under FILTER-007, and they are the module-path entry points. lakefile.lean is the package's Lean build declaration and records the mathlib dependency; it is small and gives provenance. No file meets the FILTER-004 bar for hard exclusion; disposition is retain with no rules.
